$comment: Agent-OS-owned Claude event wiring. SOURCE DATA for projectSeatHooks, never a target artifact:
the harness reads .claude/settings.json, and this file is reconciled INTO it entry-by-entry
after the Engine template hydrates. It therefore declares only the events Agent OS owns.
PreToolUse -> rgReplaceGuardHook is deliberately ABSENT: that guard is Engine-owned and tracked
(ADR 0040 2.7), so the Engine template hydrates it and the projector must preserve rather than
restate it. Restating it here would make the Brain the second author of an Engine entry.
Timeouts are part of the contract, not decoration: wakeArmingHook exports HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000
and reports before it, so a drift between that constant and the 15 below loses the report.
wakeListenerHook polls on Stop with asyncRewake: in the background, and exit 2 wakes the session
with the digest. On UserPromptSubmit it only takes the seat for the prompted session and exits,
bounded: the harness holds the prompt for it, so a poller there would block the turn it serves.
It is not on SessionStart, because a resume starts an old session that nobody may prompt, and an
owner that never reaches Stop never polls. The harness documents no timeout exemption for
asyncRewake (only for async), so the Stop entry carries an explicit day instead of the 600 s
default, which would end an idle seat's listener.
Commands are byte-identical to the pre-cut Engine template at c623b2f63c^, so the reconciliation
restores the wiring that existed rather than a re-derived approximation.
turnPresenceHook's progress beacon runs async, so no tool call waits on it; the harness enforces no
timeout on an async hook, and the writer's async MCP deadline (turnPresence.asyncHookWriteTimeoutMs)
bounds each run alone. Its start stays in the prompt's path: start opens the turn's interval, and one
landing after the turn completed would open a fresh interval for a finished turn.
PreToolUse -> harnessIdGuardHook IS ours: it refuses a call on a way into an artifact (the GitHub tools,
the shell, a written file) whose input carries the seat's own harness session id. Memory Core is our
own store and may hold that id, so its tools stay off the matcher. It is anchored because Claude tests
a matcher regex against the tool name unanchored. The hook must stay sync, because a pre-tool
decision cannot run in the background; the 2 s timeout bounds it.
